signals.signal: RBI's H1-2026 conference-call deck gives a full per-country 'business outlet' (branch) census at 30/06/2026 with the year-ago comparative: Romania 267 (from 275), Ukraine 256 (from 295), Slovakia 139 (from 141), Czechia 125 (from 127), Serbia 104 (from 105), Bosnia & Herzegovina 85 (85), Albania 74 (from 76), Hungary 68 (68), Croatia 66 (from 67), Russia 63 (from 74), Kosovo 37 (37), Poland 1, Group Corporates & Markets 19 (from 17). RBI Group total 1,304 outlets / 41,704 employees / 18.8m customers; RBI Core Group excluding Russia 1,241 outlets / 33,595 employees / 16.0m customers. The 13 unit figures sum to exactly 1,304, so the group total reconciles with no residual - unlike Erste's H1-2026 slide.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International AG, Q2/H1 2026 conference-call presentation, 'Geographic Footprint' (p.30) and Appendix country-financials tables (pp.50-64)
signals.implies: First fully reconciled group-level branch denominator for RBI. 1,241 Core-Group branches across 11 markets is the ceiling for in-branch cash automation (teller cash recyclers, assisted-service kiosks) and the base for ATM/managed-services sizing. The three biggest CEE estates - Romania 267, Ukraine 256, Slovakia 139 - are all Printec-footprint markets, and Romania is about to grow by the Garanti network rather than shrink.
signals.likelihood: High - figures are disclosed, and the branch estate is the standing denominator for any self-service or cash-automation proposal in the next 6-12 months
signals.followup: Reconcile each country figure against that subsidiary's own locator feed to derive ATM/deposit-capable counts, which RBI does not disclose at group level.

signals.signal: RBI's 2026 Core Group guidance (excluding Russia), reaffirmed with the H1 numbers on 31/07/2026: OPEX around EUR 3.8bn, cost/income ratio around 55%, net interest income above EUR 4.4bn, net fee and commission income around EUR 2.2bn, risk cost up to 35bps, consolidated RoE around 9.5%, loan growth around 7% (excluding M&A), CET1 ratio around 14.3%. H1-2026 actuals for the Core Group: OPEX EUR 1,790mn (+4% y-o-y, i.e. +3.8% on EUR 1,724mn), operating income EUR 3,382mn (+6.8%), cost/income 52.2% (down 1.6pp from 53.7%). Group-level general administrative expenses were EUR 2,152mn for 1-6/2026 vs EUR 2,033mn (+5.9%).
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International AG, Q2/H1 2026 conference-call presentation, '2026 Core Group Guidance (excl. Russia)' (p.10), 'H1/2026 Executive Summary - Core Group' (p.12) and Appendix RBI Core Group table (p.51)
signals.implies: The guided full-year OPEX of ~EUR 3.8bn against an H1 run-rate of EUR 1,790mn implies RBI has budgeted a materially heavier H2 cost load - consistent with Garanti and Addiko integration spending starting. A guided CIR of ~55% versus 52.2% delivered means RBI is explicitly accepting cost dilution, which is the window in which a vendor sells cost-take-out: managed services for ATM/self-service estates, cash-cycle automation that removes teller cost, and outsourced transaction monitoring.
signals.likelihood: High - guidance is on the record for FY2026 and will be re-tested at Q3 on 30/10/2026
signals.followup: Pull the Q3/2026 deck (financial calendar: quiet period starts 23/10/2026) to see whether OPEX guidance is revised once Garanti closing and Addiko VTO settlement land.

signals.country: Croatia, Slovenia, Austria (retained); Serbia, Bosnia & Herzegovina, Montenegro (carve-out)
signals.signal: RBI's voluntary public tender offer for all Addiko Bank shares at EUR 26.50 per share passed its 55% minimum acceptance threshold as of 29/07/2026 (preliminary, pending official results). Disclosed timeline: three-month additional acceptance period until 03/11/2026; VTO completion expected Q4/2026; carve-out closing expected H2/2027. Retained entities are Croatia, Slovenia and Austria - RBI states it would become the fourth-largest bank in Croatia and re-enter Slovenia. Serbia, Bosnia & Herzegovina and Montenegro are to be carved out, releasing an expected 35bps of RWA. One-off integration cost c. EUR 75mn spread over 2027 and 2028; CET1 impact c. -50bps initially, c. -15bps after carve-out; c. EUR 60mn profit accretion in 2028 rising through 2030.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International AG, Q2/H1 2026 conference-call presentation, 'Addiko - Voluntary Public Tender Offer and Carve-out' (p.6)
signals.implies: A dated, funded integration programme in two Printec markets. Croatia: merging Addiko Croatia into Raiffeisen Croatia (66 outlets) creates a #4 bank and forces an ATM/self-service estate rationalisation and a single-brand fleet refresh - exactly when Croatia's statutory cash-access right bites on 01/01/2027. Slovenia is a re-entry, i.e. a greenfield channel build. And the Serbia/BiH/Montenegro carve-out puts three more networks into new ownership, each of which typically re-tenders ATM managed services and monitoring. The EUR 75mn integration budget is the money that buys migration, rebranding and estate consolidation work.
signals.likelihood: High for the VTO (threshold already met); Medium-High for carve-out completing in H2/2027 subject to banking-supervisory and merger clearance
signals.followup: Watch for the official VTO result after 03/11/2026, and identify the buyer(s) of the Serbia/BiH/Montenegro carve-out - a new owner is the moment to bid managed services.

signals.signal: RBI confirmed the Garanti BBVA Romania acquisition is 'on track' with a dated integration plan: closing expected Q4/2026, legal merger expected Q4/2027, data migration and rebranding running through 2027, synergies visible from 2028. Purchase price EUR 591mn, equal to 1.28x price/book (based on H1/2025); c. -60bps CET1 impact at closing for RBI excluding Russia; one-off integration cost c. EUR 70mn mainly in 2027; c. EUR 90mn profit accretion in 2028 rising to EUR 130mn in 2030. The combined bank plus leasing company would have total assets EUR 17.5bn, loans EUR 9.9bn, deposits EUR 13.6bn, and RBI expects to become the third-largest bank in Romania by total assets.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International AG, Q2/H1 2026 conference-call presentation, 'Acquisition of Garanti BBVA Romania on Track' (p.7)
signals.implies: The single largest dated channel event in Romania. 'Data migration and rebranding' across 2027 means every acquired ATM and branch device is re-fascia'd, re-keyed and re-certified, and two self-service estates must be merged onto one switch and one monitoring stack - ATM hardware/software migration, key management/HSM re-keying, EMV/ISO re-certification, and a managed-services contract for the combined fleet. Raiffeisen Romania already runs 267 outlets; the merged entity will be the country's #3, sitting alongside BCR (Printec-served, 2,600+ ATMs) and BRD (334 branches).
signals.likelihood: High - regulatory filings under way, closing guided to Q4/2026 and merger to Q4/2027
signals.followup: Confirm Garanti BBVA Romania's own branch and ATM counts and its incumbent ATM/switch vendor, so the migration scope can be sized before the Q4/2026 closing.

signals.signal: RBI is running a full strategic review under new CEO Michael Hoellerer with a dated calendar disclosed on slide 4 of the H1-2026 deck: base-lining and preliminary review May-Jul 2026, ambition and road-map development Jul-Sep 2026, strategy update to senior management at the end of Q3/2026, kick-start of implementation from Q4/2026, and a Capital Markets Day in February 2027. Four named priorities: 'Ready for growth' (doubling down on CE and SEE), 'Focus on profitability' (13% adjusted RoE 'is just the start'; efficiency and capital allocation in the core of the business), 'Technological transformation' (product delivery - speed, scalability, independence; end-to-end process digitized and operated), and customer interaction. Hoellerer stated on 31/07/2026: 'In den kommenden Monaten werden wir intensiv an unserer neuen Strategie arbeiten, die einen klaren Fokus auf Wachstum und Profitabilitaet legen wird.'
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International AG, Q2/H1 2026 conference-call presentation, 'Priorities' (p.4); and RBI press release 'Zwischenbericht 1. Halbjahr 2026'
signals.implies: A named vendor-buying window. 'Technological transformation' plus 'end-to-end process: digitized and operated' plus 'efficiency in the core' is the standard framing under which channel/self-service estates, cash logistics and back-office processing get re-tendered or outsourced. The Feb-2027 Capital Markets Day is the moment the spend envelope becomes public; the Q4/2026 implementation kick-start is when procurement actually starts. Printec should be in front of the new Group Retail Banking head before end-Q3/2026, when the strategy goes to senior management.
signals.likelihood: High - the timetable is disclosed and dated
signals.followup: Diarise the Feb-2027 Capital Markets Day and the Q3/2026 results (quiet period from 23/10/2026, results 30/10/2026 per RBI financial calendar) for the first concrete strategy detail.

signals.entity: Raiffeisen Bank International AG / Group Retail Banking
signals.signal: RBI announced on 01/07/2026 that Curt Chadha takes over Group Retail Banking from 01/09/2026, with the mandate to drive 'die digitale Weiterentwicklung des Retailgeschaefts' and to build out partnerships, strengthening group-wide cooperation on central customer topics across RBI's core markets. Christine Anwander-Hirsch becomes head of Group Corporate Governance & Chairman's Office from 01/08/2026, with AI-supported process efficiency named among her priorities. The releases are framed as CEO Hoellerer's 'erste Schritte' in reshaping his own board portfolio.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International AG press release, 'RBI: Neue Fuehrungskraefte fuer Group Retail Banking, Generalsekretariat, Group Risk Controlling und Group Communications'
signals.implies: A new group retail owner taking office 01/09/2026, explicitly tasked with digital retail development and partnerships, is the single most addressable decision-maker change of this cycle for Printec's digital onboarding/eKYC and self-service propositions. New incumbents re-open channel and vendor questions in their first two quarters, and this one lands exactly as the group strategy is being written.
signals.likelihood: High - appointment is confirmed with a start date
signals.followup: Build the approach to Curt Chadha for Q4/2026, anchored on the 1,241-branch Core Group estate and the Garanti/Addiko migrations.

signals.entity: RBI / Raiffeisen Bankengruppe Oesterreich / European Payments Initiative (EPI)
signals.signal: EPI announced on 22/06/2026 that Erste Bank Oesterreich and the Raiffeisen Bankengruppe - RBI plus Raiffeisenlandesbank Niederoesterreich-Wien, Raiffeisenlandesbank Oberoesterreich and Raiffeisen-Landesbank Steiermark - will join EPI as new shareholders and make the Wero account-to-account payment scheme available to Austrian customers, subject to the respective supervisory-board approvals. EPI put Wero at more than 55 million users, live in Germany, Belgium and France (P2P from 2024, retail/e-commerce from end-2025), with Luxembourg (Payconiq migration, 2026) and the Netherlands (iDEAL migration, 2027) in train, and described Austria's ~9 million population as a strategic growth market.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International AG press release, 'EPI begruesst Erste Bank Oesterreich, Raiffeisen Bank International und Raiffeisen Landesbanken als neue Anteilseigner'
signals.implies: Wero is an account-to-account scheme that bypasses the card rails, and taking it to merchants means acceptance-side work: POS/terminal software updates, QR and dynamic-acceptance flows, merchant onboarding, and a second authorisation path alongside cards. For Printec's POS/acquiring and digital-onboarding lines this is a scheme-migration project of the same class as an EMV or instant-payments rollout, and RBI's CEO explicitly framed it as an offer to 'Kundinnen und Kunden sowie Haendlerinnen und Haendlern'. It also signals that RBI will eventually want Wero acceptance in its CEE markets, where it is the incumbent acquirer in several.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High for Austrian launch preparation in the next 6-12 months; timing of an Austrian consumer go-live was not disclosed
signals.followup: Track EPI/Wero Austria launch date and whether RBI extends Wero acceptance beyond Austria into its CEE subsidiaries; also confirm the supervisory-board approvals completed.

signals.signal: RBI continues to operate in Ukraine but is shrinking the physical network fast: 256 business outlets at 30/06/2026, down from 257 at 31/03/2026, 266 at 31/12/2025, 290 at 30/09/2025 and 295 at 30/06/2025 - a 13.2% year-on-year cut, the steepest of any RBI unit. Employees fell to 4,814 (from 5,135, -6.3%); customers 3.1m; loans to customers EUR 1.9bn; NPE ratio improved to 2.7% (from 3.1% at 31/12/2025) with 83.9% coverage. RBI's own commentary: the war is not expected to end before end-2026, the economy 'has increasingly evolved into a wartime economy', and Russia 'significantly intensified its attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure during the winter of 2025/2026'. Ukrainian net fee and commission income fell EUR 11mn on currency effects and 'lower earnings from clearing, settlement and payment services'; general administrative expenses fell EUR 3mn 'resulting from lower software depreciation'; the bank corporate tax rate was temporarily raised to 50 per cent. Cash in hand across Ukraine and Russia together was EUR 795mn (previous year EUR 922mn).
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International AG, Semi-Annual Financial Report 2026 (interim group management report, Ukraine segment) and Q2/H1 2026 conference-call presentation, 'Country Financials - Ukraine' (p.62)
signals.implies: Ukraine is the clearest branch-to-self-service substitution case in the group: 39 outlets closed in twelve months while customer numbers held at 3.1m. Energy-grid attacks make offline-capable, low-power, resilient self-service and cash access a survival requirement rather than an efficiency play, and remote/managed monitoring of a dispersed estate becomes essential when branches are unavailable. Note the negative read too: RBI is cutting, not investing, and named 'lower software depreciation' as a cost saving - any proposal has to be OPEX-light. Treat as a watch-and-position market rather than a near-term capex opportunity.
signals.likelihood: Medium - continued network reduction is near-certain; new vendor spend in Ukraine is unlikely before a ceasefire
signals.followup: Cross-check against NBU statistics on ATM/POS terminal counts in Ukraine (bank.gov.ua, use a desktop User-Agent) to see whether Aval's self-service estate grew as branches closed.

signals.signal: RBI restated on 31/07/2026 that run-down remains the base case in Russia, with continued ring-fencing, all restrictions on business activities to remain in place, and renewed efforts to sell. Business outlets in Russia fell to 63 at 30/06/2026 from 74 a year earlier (-14.9%) and 66 at 31/12/2025; employees fell to 8,109 from 8,657 (-6.3%); customers 2.8m. Deposits from customers in Russia are down from EUR 29.5bn in Q2/2022 to EUR 10.3bn at Q2/2026, and loans to customers (excluding C-Accounts) from EUR 13.7bn to EUR 2.5bn; equity of EUR 6.5bn now exceeds loans of EUR 2.5bn; loan/deposit ratio 23% at 30/06/2026 and LCR 471% at 24/07/2026. RBI and AO Raiffeisenbank filed the Rasperia claim on 30/07/2026 (announced 23/07/2026 as an intention to file in Austria). RBI's CET1 of 15.5% is computed on a 'P/B Zero' worst case in which the Russian unit is deconsolidated and its entire equity lost.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International AG, Q2/H1 2026 conference-call presentation, 'Russia De-Risking' (p.5) and Appendix 'Country Financials - Russia' (p.63); RBI press release 'RBI und AO Raiffeisenbank (Russland) beabsichtigen Klage gegen Rasperia in Oesterreich einzureichen'
signals.implies: Not addressable for Printec - Russia is out of the sanctions-compliant footprint - but it matters for sizing: the Core-Group-excluding-Russia numbers (1,241 outlets, 33,595 staff, 16.0m customers) are the real addressable base, and the 63 remaining Russian outlets should never be counted in a CEE opportunity. A completed sale would release capital and remove the CET1 overhang, which is what unlocks the acquisitive/investment posture behind Garanti and Addiko.
signals.likelihood: Medium - RBI has renewed sale efforts but has said run-down remains the base case
signals.followup: None for sales purposes; monitor only as a capital-release trigger for CEE investment capacity.

signals.signal: Raiffeisen Romania's own network locator feed (machine-readable AEM endpoint behind raiffeisen.ro/ro/home/retea.html), pulled 27/08/2026, returns 2,069 network points: 1,806 ATM entries and 263 branches. Of the 1,806 ATMs only 775 offer any cash-deposit service, leaving 1,031 cash-out-only. By device class the feed reports 962 plain 'Bancomat', 784 'Bancomat multifunctional' (of which 404+130+69 are flagged multifunctional EUR) and 60 'Smart Cashbox' (deposit in EUR/USD/RON/GBP for legal entities). Critically, 595 of the 1,806 ATM entries carry 'Euronet' in the device name - 414 of them plain cash-out and 181 multifunctional - i.e. roughly a third of the estate that Raiffeisen presents to customers is on a third-party independent-ATM-deployer network. The 263 branches in the feed sit just under the 267 business outlets RBI disclosed for Romania at 30/06/2026, so the feed is current. Note that Raiffeisen Romania's own SME product page still says the network is 'peste 1100 de bancomate (ATM) si masini multifunctionale (MFM)' - an undated boilerplate figure that the live feed contradicts and that should NOT be carried forward.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Romania network locator, machine-readable feed at /ro/home/retea/_jcr_content/root/container/map.maps.viewport.json (page: raiffeisen.ro/ro/home/retea.html); branch comparator from RBI Q2/H1 2026 presentation p.60
signals.implies: This is the recycler white-space number for Romania's soon-to-be #3 bank: 1,031 of 1,806 customer-facing ATMs cannot take a deposit. Every one is a candidate for replacement by a recycler or an upgrade to a deposit module - the same play quantified in Bulgaria post-euro. The 595 Euronet devices are the competitive fact: Raiffeisen has already shown it will outsource cash-out to a third party, which means a managed-services proposition is commercially acceptable to this bank but must beat an incumbent IAD on price. And the Garanti BBVA Romania integration (closing early Oct-2026, merger Q4/2027) will force a decision on the combined estate exactly in this window.
signals.likelihood: High - the estate exists and the Garanti merger forces a fleet decision through 2027
signals.followup: Pull Garanti BBVA Romania's own locator to size the incoming estate; identify who supplies and services the 1,211 non-Euronet Raiffeisen ATMs; re-pull this feed after the Oct-2026 closing - a changed count is itself the signal.

signals.signal: Raiffeisen Serbia's locator feed (same AEM pattern, behind raiffeisenbank.rs/sr/stanovnistvo/lokacije.html), pulled 27/08/2026, returns 520 network points: 417 ATMs and 103 branches. Device mix: 242 'Visenamenski uredjaj' (multifunction), 125 'Obican bankomat' (plain cash dispenser) and 50 'KUAN'. By service, 366 devices do balance enquiry, contactless acceptance and dinar dispensing; 292 accept dinar deposits; and only 206 handle EUR deposit/withdrawal. The 103 branches match the 104 business outlets RBI disclosed for Serbia at 30/06/2026.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen banka Serbia network locator, machine-readable feed at /sr/stanovnistvo/lokacije/_jcr_content/root/container/map_493090990.maps.viewport.json; branch comparator from RBI Q2/H1 2026 presentation p.61
signals.implies: Raiffeisen accounts for roughly 417 of the 3,336 ATMs the NBS counted in Serbia at Q1-2026 (~12.5%). 125 plain dispensers are direct recycler-replacement candidates, and the gap between 292 dinar-deposit devices and only 206 EUR-capable devices is a concrete upgrade line in a heavily euroised retail market. Serbia is also one of the three Addiko carve-out countries, so a second Serbian estate is about to change hands - the moment ATM managed services and monitoring typically get re-tendered.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High - device gap is real; timing tied to the Addiko carve-out (H2/2027) and normal refresh cycles
signals.followup: Compare against AikBank's machine-readable locator (aikbank.rs/data/maps-formated.json) and Banca Intesa Serbia to build a full Serbian deposit-capability league table; watch who acquires Addiko Serbia.

signals.entity: Raiffeisen Bank dd Bosna i Hercegovina / Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo J.S.C. / Raiffeisen Bank Albania
signals.signal: Locator feeds on the same AEM pattern, pulled 27/08/2026: Bosnia & Herzegovina 337 network points = 255 ATMs and 82 branches (vs 85 business outlets disclosed at 30/06/2026); Kosovo 222 points = 185 ATMs and 37 branches (matching the 37 outlets disclosed exactly); Albania's published map component returns branches only - 77 branches (vs 74 outlets disclosed) - with no ATM layer exposed on that endpoint. Kosovo's ratio of 5.0 ATMs per branch is the highest in the RBI network, against 6.9 in Romania and 4.0 in Serbia. The Bosnian and Kosovar feeds expose no deposit-capability or device-class fields, so recycler penetration in those two markets cannot be derived from the feed.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen Bank BiH locator feed (/bs/stanovnistvo/digitalni-servisi/poslovna-mreza/poslovnice-i-bankomati/_jcr_content/root/container/map.maps.viewport.json); Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo locator feed (/sq/individe/menyrat-e-bankimit/deget-dhe-atm/_jcr_content/root/container/map_copy.maps.viewport.json); Raiffeisen Bank Albania locator feed; branch comparators from RBI Q2/H1 2026 presentation pp.56-59
signals.implies: Sizes the Western Balkans piece of RBI's estate for the first time. RBI's 255 ATMs in BiH are roughly 13.7% of the 1,868 ATMs installed in BiH at 31/12/2025, and BiH is under two live pressures at once - TIPS Clone instant payments live since 20/07/2026 and FATF grey-listing since 19/06/2026 - which pull AML/transaction-monitoring and payment-rail spend forward. Kosovo's ATM-heavy, branch-light shape (185 devices, 37 branches) is already a self-service-first model and is the natural reference site for the same conversion elsewhere. RBI's #1 position in Kosovo makes it the anchor account in that market.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High - BiH regulatory clock is dated and running; Kosovo is a refresh/managed-services conversation rather than an expansion one
signals.followup: Find a deposit-capability source for BiH and Kosovo (device-level pages or CBBiH/BQK statistics via desktop User-Agent); locate the Albanian ATM layer, which is not on the published map endpoint.

signals.signal: Two dated decision points converge on 03/11/2026: RBI's Q3/2026 report and conference call are scheduled for 03 November 2026 (quiet period from 23/10/2026), and the three-month additional acceptance period for the Addiko voluntary tender offer also runs to 03 November 2026. Garanti BBVA Romania closing is expected 'Anfang Oktober' (early October 2026) per RBI's own German-language H1 release, which is more precise than the 'Q4/2026' shown on the deck. RBI's internal strategy update goes to senior management at the end of Q3/2026, with implementation kick-start in Q4/2026 and a Capital Markets Day in February 2027 (preliminary 2026 results 03/02/2027).
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International AG, Q2/H1 2026 conference-call presentation, 'Financial Calendar' (p.67) and 'Priorities' (p.4); RBI press release 'Zwischenbericht 1. Halbjahr 2026' ('Das Closing wird fuer Anfang Oktober erwartet, und die Integrationsschritte werden bereits geplant.')
signals.implies: A concrete engagement calendar. Integration planning for Garanti is stated to be under way already, so scoping conversations for the Romanian fleet migration should happen before the early-October closing, not after. The Q4/2026 strategy implementation kick-start plus the new Group Retail Banking head taking office 01/09/2026 make September-November 2026 the window in which channel and self-service decisions get framed for the Feb-2027 Capital Markets Day.
signals.likelihood: High - all dates are published by RBI
signals.followup: Diarise 03/11/2026 (Q3 results + Addiko final acceptance) and 03/02/2027 (preliminary 2026 results / Capital Markets Day window).

coverage_notes: Full fresh run - RBI Group had never been researched in a previous run (one of the eight units left blank on 30/07/2026), so everything here is is_new=true. Primary sources opened and mined locally: RBI's Q2/H1-2026 conference-call presentation (67 pages, pdfminer-extracted page by page) and the Semi-Annual Financial Report 2026 (both dated 31/07/2026), plus RBI's German-language press releases for H1 results, EPI/Wero, the Rasperia claim and the new-executive appointments. Discovered and used four previously unrecorded machine-readable locator feeds on RBI's AEM platform (pattern: <locator-page>/_jcr_content/root/.../map.maps.viewport.json) for Romania, Serbia, Bosnia and Kosovo, which is a reusable route for future runs. KEY RECONCILIATION, first time done for this group: RBI's 13 disclosed unit branch figures sum to exactly 1,304, matching the stated group total, with no residual - unlike Erste's H1-2026 slide which was 10 out. Locator branch counts corroborate the disclosure closely (Kosovo 37 vs 37, Serbia 103 vs 104, Romania 263 vs 267, BiH 82 vs 85, Albania 77 vs 74). GENUINE GAPS: (1) ISO 20022 - searched both H1 documents in full text and RBI's institutional payments/cash-management page; RBI makes NO group-level ISO 20022 or MT/MX migration disclosure, so nothing is reported rather than something inferred. (2) Croatia locator - rba.hr runs on Liferay, not AEM, and its data endpoint is inside a minified JS bundle; not recovered this run, and Croatia matters because of the Addiko merger and the 01/01/2027 statutory cash-access right. (3) Deposit-capability/device-class fields are absent from the BiH and Kosovo feeds. (4) Czechia, Slovakia and Hungary locators not pulled (Tatra banka returned 403; raiffeisen.hu sitemap exposed no locator path). (5) Addiko Group's own H1-2026 disclosure and Garanti BBVA Romania's own estate not pulled - both are the obvious next step. (6) Belarus/Priorbank not covered. DEAD FIGURE FLAGGED: Raiffeisen Romania's SME page still claims 'peste 1100 de bancomate (ATM) si masini multifunctionale' - undated boilerplate contradicted by its own live feed (1,806 ATM entries). Do not carry it forward; same failure mode as the BRD '~1,400 ATMs' figure.
access_issues: HARD CONSTRAINT: the session's WebSearch budget was already fully consumed (200/200 calls) by earlier banks before RBI was reached, so zero keyword discovery was possible for this bank. All 13 signals were obtained by direct primary-source fetching with a desktop User-Agent plus local pdfminer text extraction - no aggregator was used and no source is second-hand. Blocked/awkward URLs and the routes used: rbinternational.com/sitemap.xml is stale (lastmod Aug-2025) and the press-release index is JS-rendered - recovered the underlying AEM feed at /de/raiffeisen/media-hub/presseaussendungen/2026/_jcr_content/root/container/newslist_copy_copy.newssearch.{n}.json, which returned the complete 2026 release list. www.tatrabanka.sk/sitemap.xml returned 403 even with a desktop User-Agent - logged, not worked around. www.rba.hr locator is Liferay-rendered and its endpoint was not recoverable from the HTML - logged. Guessed locator paths on raiffeisen.ro, rba.hr and raiffeisenbank.rs returned 404 before the correct AEM endpoints were found via each site's sitemap.xml. No source was silently dropped.
operator_requests: none - every document needed was publicly reachable. If a future run wants Croatia device-level data, an operator or Claude-in-Chrome session on https://www.rba.hr/lokacije-poslovnice-bankomati would capture the XHR the Liferay bundle fires, which this run could not reach headlessly.
